1_adc_hazard.why: Every live launch goes through AiBridge.live_plan (bridge/ai_bridge.gd:259-271), which always appends --ai-no-adc (line 267) and, only when a Gemini key file is present, --ai <image> --ai-key-file <that file> (lines 268-269); the OpenRouter-only launch binds no std/ai at all. Both source-checkout and exported-build launch paths call live_plan (launch_plan lines 290-291 and 297-298); the stub path (_run_args) has --caps IO,FS and no --ai. No Makefile target runs the live entry with Net or AI capabilities: the ai_live macro (mk/ai.mk:127) runs --entry live under $(AI_NOKEYS) with --caps IO,FS,Env only, and ai-loopback (mk/ai.mk:156-157) calls the adapters directly against 127.0.0.1 with fake keys and env -u AI_LIVE. ailang v0.52.0 documents --ai-no-adc as 'a missing GOOGLE_API_KEY is a hard AuthFailed error' and --ai-key-file as the key for the --ai provider, never echoed; I confirmed --ai-no-adc is accepted without --ai (stub session hello rc 0), and test_ai_relay's key-hygiene cases spawn real ailang for both/gemini-only/openrouter-only key sets with both flags asserted. TTS and the AI_LIVE refusal read GOOGLE_API_KEY from the env (x-goog-api-key header, ai/adapters.ail:84), which the wrapper fills from the key file: no ADC path there. The wrapper also keeps GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/nonexistent. Residual (not verified, needs the user): in a source checkout HOME is Godot's real HOME (live_plan default), so if ailang reads an AI credential from ~/.ailang/config.yaml it would be reachable; --ai-key-file is explicit and should win, and the evaluator did not inspect that file's contents (credential exploration is out of bounds for this agent). An attended run can remove the doubt by pointing HOME at a scratch directory with only the package cache.

2_billed_unparsable_replies.why: billedOpenRouter and billedTts (ai/reply.ail:104-115, 161-165) return Some(tokens) for any body that decodes and has no top-level 'error', so a 200 with usage but no content, finish_reason error inside choices, a Gemini candidate blocked with usageMetadata, and speech over its cap are all charged with one call plus the reported tokens (ai/adapters.ail:65 and 88), and provider.failed appends the usage line and charges the ledger (ai/provider.ail:221-226). Proven on the loopback (/nocontent 312+27 tokens -> 7320 nano-USD, /capped -> 1192000 nano-USD, usage.ndjson lines b1/b12 with usd > 0) and by three killed mutants plus mine (tokensIn forced to 0 -> reply_test fails). Escapes found: (a) an HTTP transport Err (timeout after send, connection reset) is Err('provider_error') with units unchanged (adapters.ail:63, 86), so a reply the provider billed but never delivered is uncharged; (b) worse, the bridge's per-kind timeout (voice 60 s, portrait 120 s) kills the service mid-call, so neither the ledger nor usage.ndjson sees that call, and the restarted service starts a fresh ledger (service.ail:183). Both are bounded in an attended run by the player watching the indicator and by the small ceiling, so they do not block AI.10b; they should be closed before any unattended or player-facing live use (charge the request's cap on a transport error; carry the session's spend into the relaunch config).

3_env_i_minimal_environment.why: LIVE_WRAP (bridge/ai_bridge.gd:63) execs /usr/bin/env -i with only PATH, HOME, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/nonexistent and, iff the permission argument is exactly '1', AI_LIVE=1; the inner /bin/sh -c reads each key file with a quoted "$1"/"$2" and exports the variable, then shift 2; exec "$@" (same pid). No key is in any argv: only the two file paths and the --ai-key-file path. test_live_env runs this with a real spawn and an env-dumping stand-in for ailang: FOO_API_KEY and an inherited GOOGLE_API_KEY do not reach the child, the keys come from the files, AI_LIVE only with permission 1; the env -i and the AI_LIVE gate each have a killed bridge mutant. I exercised the wrapper directly with a key directory named 'kdir with space/$x'q' and a key value containing $HOME, backticks and a quote: the key arrived byte for byte, the --ai-key-file argument kept the path intact, permission 0 and permission 'yes' both left AI_LIVE unset, and an empty Gemini path exported no GOOGLE_API_KEY. This matters because the real macOS user:// is '.../Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/Stapledon's Voyage/' (space and apostrophe), which test_live_env's scratch path does not cover (own_mutations.survived: an unquoted cat $1 survives the test). FD_SCRUB closes inherited descriptors before the exec, so the service sees no sim pipe.

4_ai_live_guard.why: Runtime defences, in order: (1) the service refuses before any call unless AI_LIVE=1 and a routed key are in its env (service.ail:146, 180); (2) the only path that puts AI_LIVE=1 in a service env is LIVE_WRAP with permission '1', which live_plan derives from AiBridge.live_allowed only; (3) live_allowed defaults to false and, outside tests, is written only in AiSettings.apply from live_on() = opt_in and not automation and a key present (ai_settings.gd:136-137, 189-193), both asserted statically by rules D and E and dynamically by test_launch_default; (4) automation is true for --capture, --map-capture, --golden, --bench and --ai-hello, and --capture/--golden/--bench never reach _run_map at all (main.gd:62-66: only --map/--map-capture construct an AiSession), so make capture, make golden, make bench, make map-capture and make export-smoke cannot go live whatever user://ai_settings.cfg holds; (5) with live off the relay is 'off' and no service starts. Tests set live_allowed only to false (rule B forbids 'live_allowed = true' in tests/ and tools/). Static rules A-E caught every spelling the sprint named plus the 10 shipped mutants and my GDScript launch_override with an env AI_LIVE=1 wrapper. Evasions I found (adversarial_probes.guard_evasions): rule A's regex misses '--entry  live' (two spaces), '--entry "live"', '--entry $(E)' with E := live, and does not scan .py at all, so a Python harness with env={"AI_LIVE": "1"} also passes rule C (which wants AI_LIVE immediately followed by = or :); and a recipe line can be exempted by ending it with the mutant-table suffix "# @A x' \". Each of these still needs a real key in the make environment, which CI and the unattended loop do not have, and the automation flags plus the live_allowed gate hold regardless. Harden before AI.10b adds its own exception (see non_blocking_findings).

deviation_verdicts.guard_matches_entry_live_and_non_stub_pr: ACCEPT. Under the AI.5 wire the provider is the entry plus its argument, so '--provider gemini' alone would be a dead rule; the guard matches --entry live, --provider gemini|openrouter and a non-stub "provider" in the entry argument, and the two --provider mutants the sprint demanded are both caught. The matching is literal (see guard_evasions), which is a hardening item, not a reason to reject the widened rule.

deviation_verdicts.only_galaxy_map_wired: ACCEPT. The galaxy map is the default game (main.gd:60-62) and the only surface with ai_request events; the --voyage flight has no conversation UI, and AI.10a's conversation scene is its own scene. Recorded in the as-built section.

deviation_verdicts.import_keep_files_force_added: ACCEPT. *.import is gitignored (.gitignore:3), so -f is the only way to track the 8 three-line 'keep' files, and without them the export re-imports the stub PNGs as textures and the stub cannot read them (the executor hit this; my export confirms the stub starts). ai-core-bundle writes the same keep files for the core blobs.

deviation_verdicts.unpack_marker_is_a_digest: ACCEPT, with a gap to close: a digest beats the old boolean (an older unpack is refreshed and the cache re-copied), but it hashes only the lock, three data tables and service.ail while the root is keyed by the runtime version, so a build that changes another ai/*.ail module or a fixture with the same service.ail would not re-unpack (adversarial_probes.unpack_digest). Hash every bundled ai/ file (or the export's own build id) instead.

deviation_verdicts.indicator_uses_usage_ndjson: ACCEPT. Error results carry no meta.usd, so summing meta.usd would miss exactly the charged failures AI.9 set out to count; the usage lines are the service's own ledger entries and test_indicator_budget pins per-provider and total sums. The sprint text's 'meta.usd' was the mechanism, not the requirement.

deviation_verdicts.openrouter_images_unsupported_on_v0_52_0: ACCEPT. The decision point was re-checked at the bump and the default (portraits Gemini-only, routing table unchanged) stands; nothing in this milestone depends on it.

non_blocking_findings: ai/service.ail:183 and bridge/ai_session.gd:71-74: the spend ledger is per service process. Every settings change restarts the service (shutdown when idle, lazy relaunch) and every fault/timeout restarts it after backoff, each time with ledgerOf(ceiling_usd) at zero, so the player's ceiling bounds one process, not the session; only the indicator's usage.ndjson sum is session-wide. Fix before any unattended or player-facing live use: have AiSession pass the session's spent total (the indicator's sum, or a session id the service uses to replay this session's usage lines) into the live config and start the ledger from it; add a test that a relaunch after a budget refusal is still refused.

ai/adapters.ail:63 and :86 (transport Err -> units unchanged) and bridge/ai_bridge.gd:461-466 (_timeout kills the child mid-call): a request the provider billed but that timed out or was killed leaves no usage line and no ledger charge, so both the ceiling and the indicator under-count. Charge the request's cap (textCap/ttsCap, or the portrait per_call) on a transport error, and let the bridge append a provisional usage line for a killed in-flight live request.

tools/ai_live_guard.sh:42 (rule A) and :56 (rule C): literal matching. Normalise whitespace before matching, treat any '--entry' whose value is not a literal non-live word (variables, quotes) as live, scan .py and .gd for the live entry and for AI_LIVE in dict/mapping form ('AI_LIVE"? *[:=]'), and drop the suffix exemption in favour of exempting the mutant tables by line range or by file. Five evasions listed in adversarial_probes.guard_evasions.

tests/test_ai_settings.gd: add 'automation run -> indicator == null' (MG2 survived), 'usage lines before _ready are not counted' (MG3 survived), and 'an empty or whitespace-only key file is no key' (MG1 survived).

bridge/ai_bridge.gd:304-323 _unpack_ai: extend the digest to every file copied (all ai/*.ail, ai/fixtures/*, data/ai/*) or key the root by a build id, so a rebuilt export with the same runtime version and service.ail does not run stale modules.

tools/ai_live_guard.sh:68 rule E walks '.' with find -maxdepth 4; in the main checkout that includes .claude/worktrees/*/bridge/*.gd and */main.gd. Use git ls-files so other checkouts under the repo can never make the guard pass or fail.

on every apply and removed only in AiSession._exit_tree; a crash leaves it behind (0600, same protection as a saved key). Remove stale session files at startup too.

mk/ai.mk:441 ai-export-smoke and Makefile:189 export-smoke run the exported app with HOME=$HOME, so the smoke reads and writes the real user:// (ai_cache under 'Stapledon's Voyage'); harmless with --ai-hello (automation), but a scratch HOME would keep the player's data out of a test.

Design doc 'AI.9 as built' and the sprint JSON notes should record the per-process ledger and the transport-error gap, so AI.10b's attended run plans its ceiling with them in mind (e.g. make ai-live keeps --ceiling-usd low and Mark watches the indicator, which is session-wide).
evaluator_notes: Merge-ready from the evaluator's side; CI is green at the evaluated commit. The four must-fix items each hold for an attended live run (must_fix_verdicts), with the ledger restart and the timeout-after-send as the two residuals to carry into AI.10a/AI.10b planning. The evaluator did not look inside ~/.ailang/config.yaml (credential exploration is out of bounds); the user should confirm it carries no AI credential that ailang would read under Godot's HOME, or point the attended run's HOME at a scratch directory. Scratch artefacts (mutant copies, the guard-evasion copy, the wrapper probe, the exported .app, the fetched sky textures and core blobs) live only in the session scratchpad clone and are not part of the branch; the clone's tree is clean apart from this report.
